scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

Even though the Switch is the user's property, the stepbrother might have had a reasonable expectation that his save data would be preserved, especially since he was using it with permission.

But wait, the user said they made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up their saves. So the stepbrother's profile was on the user's device. If the user owns the device, they can delete profiles. However, deleting someone else's save data without warning could be seen as disrespectful, especially if they knew the stepbrother was using it and had progress. Even if it's their property, there's a social aspect here. The stepbrother was relying on that save, and deleting it caused emotional distress.

But is it morally wrong? Let's consider intent. The user deleted it because they were annoyed by having to switch profiles each time. So it was a convenience thing for themselves. But they didn't consider the impact on the stepbrother. The stepbrother was enjoying playing it, and the save was important to him. So even though the user owns the Switch, deleting someone else's save data without notice is inconsiderate. Especially since the stepbrother was using it with permission during that time. But technically, the data is stored on the device, which the user owns. However, in terms of moral responsibility, even if you own the device, deleting someone else's data without consent is generally considered wrong. For example, if someone uses your computer and you delete their files, even if it's your computer, it's still a breach of trust.

In this case, the stepbrother was using the Switch with permission, and the user created a profile for him. So the stepbrother had a right to expect that his save data would be preserved. Deleting it without warning, especially when he was relying on it, is inconsiderate. The fact that the user didn't think it was a big deal because they don't usually bring the Switch over doesn't matter because during that week, the stepbrother was using it. The user should have either kept the profile or informed him before deleting it.

So morally, it's unacceptable. The action caused harm (emotional distress, loss of progress) without justification. Even though the Switch is the user's property, they have a responsibility to respect others' data when they've allowed them to use it. So the answer should be 0.
